paper.title: Wind Farm Layout Optimization on Complex Terrains - Integrating a CFD Wake Model with Mixed-Integer Programming

target_contribution: iterative two-way coupling between exact/near-exact discrete MIP layout selection and newly promising single-turbine CFD wake rows
paper_lifecycle: construct approximate wake rows by applying terrain speed-up to a flat-terrain row
solve the MIP for twenty cells
simulate single-turbine wakes at newly selected cells
replace those cells' approximate wake rows with simulated rows
repeat until no newly promising cell is selected

figure_proxy.terrain: twenty-by-twenty sampling of Figure 4 against its printed 20 m colorbar bands
figure_proxy.wind: normalized radial-length digitization of the twelve Figure 5 bars

mip_backend.name: HiGHS
mip_backend.linearization: for every nonzero pair coefficient y_ij=x_i*x_j is enforced by y<=x_i, y<=x_j, and x_i+x_j-y<=1
mip_backend.result_policy: record model status, incumbent, dual bound, and gap; never call a time-limited incumbent globally optimal

missing_information: author 20x20 terrain and numeric wind-rose arrays
no-turbine and 4800 possible single-turbine CFD fields
flat-terrain wake field and mesh/boundary solution arrays
Gurobi model/source, exact solver settings, and warm starts
final cell arrays and per-iteration objective histories

reconstruction.background: digitized elevation plus printed power-law Eq. 5
reconstruction.initial_row: declared straight Jensen wake using printed CT and geometry
reconstruction.replacement_row: declared terrain-aware single-turbine surrogate with slope-driven turn, expansion, and vertical separation
reconstruction.important_boundary: the replacement row exercises the CFD-to-MIP information lifecycle but is not labeled CFD or author data
reconstruction.finite_termination_bound: at most 400 locations can become newly known; one final solve establishes that no new location remains

hpc_contract.field_parallel_axis: 400 independent source-cell rows, each aggregating 400 targets and twelve sectors
hpc_contract.mip_parallelism: each HiGHS solve receives its relaxation case worker partition; five independent cases execute concurrently
hpc_contract.storage: contiguous source-major approximate and terrain-aware pair arrays
hpc_contract.formal_axis: five independent relaxation cases run concurrently; the available Waffle cores are partitioned across cases while each case preserves its sequential CFD-MIP lifecycle
hpc_contract.full_resource_policy: partition the entire Waffle CPU allocation across the five independent cases without nested oversubscription

claim_boundary: academic declared reproduction of equations, discrete problem, relaxation study, exact MILP linearization, and iterative update lifecycle on a figure/surrogate proxy; not author CFD, Gurobi, or numerical replay
